title: Later notes from S258 and S274: daemon and CLI
lead: Follow-ups raised by the reviewers, UI passes and gates of S258 and S274. Each is unverified beyond the review that raised it; re-anchor before work. *Proposed.*
findings_note: S258 and S274 reviews and gates, 2026-11-07

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
Follow-ups raised by the reviewers, UI passes and gates of S258 and S274 (2026-11-07), and the S265/S306 note on this item. Every item was re-anchored against main on 2026-11-18; the ones still open are below, the dropped ones after them. The CLI items touch `internal/cli` output, so the slice gets a UI pass (rule u10). The TUI items T1-T6 moved to S449 (owner, 2026-11-18: split S307).

Still open, daemon and CLI:

- A1. The `no_spec_check_row` fix lines build `ork projects set NAME ...` with the bare name (`internal/daemon/speccheck.go:165`, `internal/daemon/speccheck.go:177`). Registry names are checked only for non-empty (`internal/registry/registry.go:424-425`), so a name with a space gives a command that cannot be pasted. The TUI already quotes with `engine.ShellWord` (`internal/tui/launch.go:567-569`, `internal/engine/setup.go:63`).
- A2. `matrixUse` labels any row listed in the spec check row set "Spec check row", whatever its role (`internal/daemon/matrix.go:203-209`), but the plan leaves out only reviewer-sourced rows (`internal/daemon/runs.go:648-650`), and `specChain` reads only reviewer rows (`internal/daemon/speccheck.go:208-210`). An implementer row id in `spec_check_rows` is labelled a Spec check row and still runs as an implementer.
- A3. A row in both the UI pass set and the spec check set: the plan drops it as a spec check row first (`internal/daemon/runs.go:648-656`), the matrix labels it "UI pass row" first (`internal/daemon/matrix.go:204-207`).
- A4. `spec_check_rows` that take every reviewer row leave the reviewer chain empty, and `planRun` returns a plain `fmt.Errorf` ("lineup has no row with an adapter for reviewer", `internal/daemon/runs.go:666-671`) that has no ipc code, so the owner sees it as internal.
- A5. Stale comments: `SpecCheckRows` says unset means "the row that the Spec check row rule names" (`internal/registry/registry.go:278-281`), but it is every row any rule names, in rule order (`internal/daemon/speccheck.go:105-115`); the `matrixUse` comment says the UI pass and Spec check rows are rows "that a rule names" (`internal/daemon/matrix.go:182-186`), but project settings name them too.
- B1. `ork answer --wait` and `ork retry --wait` return at once when the resume waits for a slot: the stored-resume path returns before the `NoWait` check (`internal/daemon/runs.go:2433-2449` against `internal/daemon/runs.go:2453-2458`). Decided: wait (adj 472, `cli.wait-queued-resume`); `--wait` waits until the stored resume starts and the run rests again.
- B2. A stop that cancels an answer already filed in adj: the reply is the job's `context canceled` error (`internal/daemon/runs.go:2484-2490`), and the client shows the error, not the filing notice carried in `Message`.
- B3. The waiting-path adj filing runs under the request context (`fileWaitingAnswerLocked(ctx, ...)`, `internal/daemon/runs.go:2117-2121`), so a client that disconnects can leave a key asked but not decided.
- C1. `ork projects set --allow` adds patterns (adj 190), but the summary prints only each role's total pattern count (`internal/cli/daemoncmds.go:756-771`, `internal/cli/daemoncmds.go:787-791`), not how many were added or were already listed.
- C2. An older TUI or CLI binary against a restarted daemon gets "plan changed; run the command again to confirm it" (`internal/daemon/runs.go:1056`, `internal/daemon/runs.go:1156`) on any plan with warnings. No upgrade note says so.

Dropped on 2026-11-18, with evidence:

- `spec_check_rows` after a shared matrix renumbers rows: S261 (open, "Shared role matrix") rewrites row ids in the target project; it belongs there.
- A failed registry read admits answer and retry on the last good file: the same rule as every queued start (`loadRunRegistryLocked`, `internal/daemon/runs.go:1819-1826`, used by `launchRun` at `internal/daemon/runs.go:2178-2182`). No change.
- `engineRuns` reads the registry once per waiting run under the manager lock (`internal/daemon/runs.go:2794`): cost only, no observed problem.
- "Long refusal and status lines overflow 80 columns with real run ids": no line named beyond T3, and the review called them consistent with existing ones.
- `TestDoctorCheckCommandSyntaxError` on Linux: it passes on this Linux host on 2026-11-18 (it lowercases the output, `internal/cli/cli_test.go:1039-1044`).
- The Codex implementer's missing host binary: host setup, not ork code.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
Each item was re-anchored on 2026-11-18. At step 1, a test that is already green means a later slice fixed that item: drop the test and the item and say so in the report.

Daemon and CLI:

- `TestNoSpecCheckRowQuotesTheProjectName` in `internal/daemon/speccheck_test.go`: `noSpecCheckRow` for a project named `my proj`, with and without rows set; every `ork projects set` line reads `ork projects set 'my proj' ...`. Red today: the name is bare (A1).
- `TestMatrixLabelsOnlyReviewerRowsAsSpecCheckRows` in `internal/daemon/matrix_test.go`: `matrixUse` for an implementer row whose id is in the spec row set is not labelled "Spec check row"; a reviewer row with the same id set is. Red today (A2).
- `TestMatrixLabelsARowInBothListsAsTheSpecCheckRow` in `internal/daemon/matrix_test.go`: a reviewer row in both the UI and the spec sets is labelled "Spec check row", as the plan uses it. Red today: "UI pass row" (A3).
- `TestPlanWhoseSpecCheckRowsTakeEveryReviewerRowIsRefused` in `internal/daemon/runs_test.go`: `spec_check_rows` listing every reviewer row; `planRun` returns an `*ipc.Error` with code `refused` whose message names `spec_check_rows`. Red today: a plain error (A4).
- `TestAnswerWaitOnAQueuedResume` in `internal/daemon/runs_test.go`: adj 472 (wait): with no free slot and `NoWait` false, the answer's reply does not come back until the stored resume has started and the run rests again. Red today: it returns at once with `resume waits for a slot` (B1).
- `TestStopDuringAnAnsweredRoundKeepsTheFilingNotice` in `internal/daemon/runs_test.go`: an answer with `Adj` filed, then `ork stop` while `engine.Answer` runs; the answer's reply is ok and its message reads `run RUN was stopped; answer filed in adj as #N`. Red today: the reply is `context canceled` (B2).
- `TestWaitingAnswerFilingOutlivesTheRequest` in `internal/daemon/runs_test.go`: a fake adj whose decide blocks; the request context is cancelled during the filing; the key ends decided. Red today: the filing runs under the request context (B3).
- `TestProjectsSetAllowSaysAddedAndAlreadyListed` in `internal/cli/cli_test.go`: `--allow implementer=A --allow implementer=B` where B is already listed prints `implementer: 1 pattern added, 1 already listed` in the summary. Red today: only the total count (C1).

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. Write the failing tests and see each red for the stated reason. Drop any item whose test is already green, as Failing tests says.
2. A1: build both `ork projects set` lines in `noSpecCheckRow` with `engine.ShellWord(proj.Name)`.
3. A2, A3: make `matrixUse` label what the plan does: "Spec check row" only for a reviewer row, and the spec check label before the UI pass label. A5: fix the two comments.
4. A4: when the reviewer chain is empty and some reviewer rows were left out as spec check rows, return `&ipc.Error{Code: CodeRefused}` naming those rows and `spec_check_rows`, with the fix `ork projects set NAME --spec-check-rows ...`.
5. B1: adj 472 (wait), scoped by adj 511 (cli-only). Add a wire field to `RunAction`, `wait_queued`, that only `ork answer --wait` and `ork retry --wait` set. With it, when the stored resume waits for a slot, the reply waits until the resume has started and the run rests again. Without it (the TUI, `Client.AnswerAction` and `Client.RetryAction`) the reply is `resume waits for a slot` at once, as today.
6. B2: when the owner's stop cancels an answer whose adj filing succeeded, reply ok with the message `run RUN was stopped; answer filed in adj as #N`.
7. B3: run the waiting-path filing under the manager's context (`d.runs.ctx`), not the request's.
8. C1 (adj 512, wrapper): `project.set` returns a new result type, `SetProjectResult`, holding the `registry.Project` plus per-role `added` and `already_listed` pattern lists; `Client.SetProject` returns it, `--json` prints it, and the CLI summary prints both counts. The counts are not saved in the registry file.
9. Docs: `docs/design.md` (A1-A4, B1-B3, C1), `docs/guide.md` upgrade note (C2: a client older than the daemon may see "plan changed" on a plan with warnings, and cannot read the new `project.set` reply of adj 512; upgrade both). Changelog entry with `slicer changelog add S307 --text "..."`.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
Acceptance criteria:
- Every ork projects set line in the no spec check row error can be pasted for a project name with a space.
- The role matrix labels a row as the plan uses it, and a spec check row setting that empties the reviewer chain is refused with a fix, not shown as internal.
- ork answer and ork retry with --wait behave on a queued resume as adj 472 decided: they wait until the stored resume starts and the run rests again.
- A stop during a filed answer reports the filing; a waiting-path filing finishes when the client goes away.
- ork projects set --allow says how many patterns were added and how many were already listed.

Commands:
- `go test ./internal/daemon -run 'TestNoSpecCheckRowQuotesTheProjectName|TestMatrixLabels|TestPlanWhoseSpecCheckRowsTakeEveryReviewerRowIsRefused|TestAnswerWaitOnAQueuedResume|TestStopDuringAnAnsweredRoundKeepsTheFilingNotice|TestWaitingAnswerFilingOutlivesTheRequest' -v`
- `go test ./internal/cli -run 'TestProjectsSetAllowSaysAddedAndAlreadyListed' -v`
- `go vet ./...`
- `go test ./...`
- `go test -race ./internal/daemon`
- `gofmt -l .` prints nothing.
- `slicer check` exits 0.
- `adj lint` exits 0.
